waveName: Wave 2 – Workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours & preview, photo intake, design system

package.title: APK saves visibly, back button, safe areas, WebView guard, crash recovery
package.goal: In the APK the user always learns where a PDF, CSV or backup went, or that saving failed, and can share it again. The back button behaves like Android expects. System bars stay readable. Outdated WebViews get an explanation instead of a blank screen. A renderer crash reloads instead of killing the app.
steps:
platform.ts saveNative returns {savedPath:string|null, cacheUri, shared:boolean, error?:string}.
- Record Documents write errors instead of swallowing them.
- Treat a cancelled Share as shared=false, not as an error.
- Encode in chunks of 3 MiB, a multiple of 3 bytes. Call writeFile then appendFile into Cache, then Filesystem.copy to Documents/MosaicPlan, then stat and compare the size.
- Export timestampedName(base, ext) and reshare(cacheUri).

components.tsx: downloadBlob returns that SaveResult; on the web it returns {kind:'download'}. SaveResultNote (role=status) shows 'Gespeichert: Dokumente/MosaicPlan/<name>' ONLY when savedPath is set. Otherwise it shows a warning with the reason and a 'Teilen' button.
Projects.tsx: await export, duplicate and delete inside try/catch and show errors. On native, give backup files a timestamp in the name. Show SaveResultNote after export.

AndroidManifest: READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE with maxSdkVersion 29, and android:requestLegacyExternalStorage="true". MainActivity: register a WebViewListener whose onRenderProcessGone reloads the bridge WebView and returns true.

Back button: add @capacitor/app ^8.1 and run npx cap sync. In main.tsx, when isNative(): App.addListener('backButton', ({canGoBack}) => canGoBack ? history.back() : App.minimizeApp()). This relies on the wave-1 modal history and the wave-2 route-driven steps.

System bars: in capacitor.config set plugins.SystemBars.initialViewportFitValueHint='cover'. In main.tsx add an env(safe-area-inset-top) probe with a ResizeObserver. If the inset is > 0, set the StatusBar style to Dark and the NavigationBar style to Light; otherwise use Default. All calls are wrapped in .catch.

WebView guard:
- vite.config: build.target ['chrome111','edge111','firefox114','safari16.4'].
- capacitor.config: android.minWebViewVersion 111 and server.errorPath 'webview-update.html'.
- public/webview-update.html: ES5, de/en/tr. Parse the Chrome version from the user agent. Below 111, show update instructions with market:// and https Play links; otherwise show a generic load-error message.
- index.html: an inline ES5 probe of syntax (??=, ||=, class fields), structuredClone and module workers. On failure it replaces #root with the message and sets a flag that main.tsx respects.
acceptance: Unit test with a mocked @capacitor/filesystem: a rejected Documents write gives savedPath null, and the UI renders the warning, not a path. Chunked base64 pieces decode back to the original bytes.
Playwright: deleting window.structuredClone via addInitScript shows the update message, and the root is not blank.
`npx cap sync android` succeeds and capacitor.plugins.json lists App.
package.risk: Effort M. A browser cannot test native behaviour; mark it device-unverified in the README in wave 7. Do not use exitApp.

findings.title: APK file saving gives no feedback and fails silently on Android 10; after the share sheet the user cannot find or reopen the PDF/CSV/backup
findings.problem: saveNative (platform.ts:20-36) tries Directory.Documents and silently swallows any failure. It returns savedPath, but downloadBlob ignores it (components.tsx:157-160). Callers do not await it (StepPdf.tsx:73, StepPlan.tsx:48, Projects.tsx:76), so errors become unhandled rejections. On native the 'Öffnen' link is hidden (StepPdf.tsx:182), and the only message is 'PDF erstellt (x KB).' The Filesystem plugin's own README says Directory.Documents on Android 10 and older needs READ+WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE. The manifest declares only WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE with maxSdkVersion=28, no READ, and no requestLegacyExternalStorage, so on Android 10 (API 29) the Documents write is rejected and only the share sheet remains. If the user dismisses it, the file exists only in the app cache. This matters especially for project export, which README names as the only protection against data loss when reinstalling.
findings.evidence: Code: src/platform.ts:22-27 (try writeFile Documents, catch {}), src/ui/components.tsx:158-160 ('await saveNative(blob, name); return;' with the result unused), android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml (only WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE maxSdkVersion=28), node_modules/@capacitor/filesystem/README.md lines 114-123 ('in Android 10 and older, this API requires ... READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE ... WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE'), and FilesystemPlugin.kt:408-416 (below API 30 it requires the PUBLIC_STORAGE alias = READ+WRITE). The i18n string 'pdfui.done' (de.ts:402) gives no location. Not testable on a device here; the conclusion comes from the plugin source and docs.
findings.proposal: 1) Make downloadBlob return {savedPath, shared, error} and await it everywhere. Show an inline success line or toast: 'Gespeichert: Dokumente/MosaicPlan/<name>' or 'Konnte nicht in Dokumente speichern – bitte über Teilen sichern'. 2) On native, replace the hidden 'Öffnen' link with 'Erneut teilen/öffnen', which calls Share.share({files:[cacheUri]}) again. 3) Quick manifest fix: WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE with maxSdkVersion="29" plus android:requestLegacyExternalStorage="true" on <application>. 4) Robust option: a ~40-line custom plugin in MainActivity that opens Intent.ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT (system 'Speichern unter' dialog, no permissions needed on API 24-36) and writes the bytes to the returned Uri. Use it for 'Projekt sichern' and 'PDF speichern'.
corrected:
1) src/platform.ts: make saveNative return `{ savedPath: string; cacheUri: string; shared: boolean; error?: string }`.
- Record the Documents writeFile error message instead of using an empty catch.
- Treat Share's 'Share canceled' rejection as shared=false, not as an error.
- Let real failures (blobToBase64, Cache write) propagate.

2) src/ui/components.tsx:157: make downloadBlob return that result; on the web return `{ savedPath: '', shared: false }`. Await it at all four call sites: StepPdf.tsx:73, StepPlan.tsx:48, Projects.tsx:76 and Materials.tsx:114, the last one missing from the original finding. Wrap each call in try/catch that shows the error.
- In StepPdf, call setResult only after the save resolves.
- On native, show one of two messages:
  - 'Gespeichert: Dokumente/MosaicPlan/<name>' when savedPath is set.
  - A warning badge 'Nicht in Dokumente gespeichert – bitte über Teilen sichern (<reason>)' when it is not.
- Add i18n keys in de/en/tr.

3) Replace the hidden 'Öffnen' link (StepPdf.tsx:182) with an 'Erneut teilen' button that calls Share.share({ files: [cacheUri] }). Use the same button for the CSV and project export messages.
- Projects.tsx export also needs a visible confirmation. It currently has none.
- Optionally add a timestamp to the backup file name so an older backup is not silently overwritten.

4) AndroidManifest.xml quick fix: declare WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, both with maxSdkVersion="29", and set android:requestLegacyExternalStorage="true" on <application>.
- Android 7-10 will then show a storage permission prompt on the first export. Point 2 must handle a denial with the warning message.
- On API 30+ the plugin does not request permissions for Directory.Documents writes (isStoragePermissionGranted(false) returns true), so the maxSdkVersion cap is safe for the app's current calls.

5) Robust option for 'Projekt sichern' and 'PDF speichern': a small custom Capacitor plugin (Java, registered in MainActivity via registerPlugin(SaveAsPlugin.class) before super.onCreate).
- It launches Intent.ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT with the right MIME type and suggested name. This is the system 'Speichern unter' dialog and needs no permissions on API 24-36.
- In the activity result it stream-copies the already-written cache file (cacheUri from point 1) into the returned content Uri via ContentResolver.openOutputStream. Do not pass the base64 payload over the bridge a second time, which matters for large PDFs.
- Return the chosen display name so the UI can confirm where the file was saved.

1) Report the real outcome of every save (src/platform.ts, src/ui/components.tsx):
- Change saveNative to return `{ savedPath: string | null, cacheUri: string, shared: boolean, error?: string }`. Set `savedPath` only when Filesystem.writeFile to Documents actually resolved. On failure, keep the error message. Set `shared` from the Share.share result (it rejects when dismissed).
- downloadBlob returns `Promise<SaveResult>` (on the web: `{ kind: 'download' }`).

2) Await the save in all four callers, inside their existing try/catch: StepPdf.tsx:73, StepPlan.tsx:48, Projects.tsx:76 and Materials.tsx:114. A failure then shows up as an error instead of an unhandled rejection under a success message.

3) Add a small shared status line component (role="status", aria-live="polite") in components.tsx. New i18n keys in de, en and tr:
- Success: "Gespeichert: Dokumente/MosaicPlan/<name>". Show it only when `savedPath` is set; never claim a location that was not written.
- Failure: "Nicht in Dokumente gespeichert (<Grund>). Bitte über Teilen sichern." plus a "Teilen" button.

4) On native, replace the hidden "Öffnen" link (StepPdf.tsx:182) with a "Teilen / Öffnen" button. Keep `cacheUri` in component state and call Share.share({ files: [cacheUri] }) again. Do the same after project export in Projects.tsx.

5) Avoid name collisions on native. Add a timestamp suffix to exported file names, e.g. `<name>_2026-11-07_1432.mosaicplan.json` and `_verlegeplan_<ts>.pdf`. If writeFile still fails, retry once with a `_2` suffix. Without this, a backup written after a reinstall on Android 11+ fails silently because the old file belongs to the previous installation.

6) Manifest fix for Android 10 (android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml), as required by the Filesystem plugin README and FilesystemPlugin.kt:410-416:
- `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE" android:maxSdkVersion="29"/>`
- Change WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE to maxSdkVersion="29".
- Add `android:requestLegacyExternalStorage="true"` on `<application>`. Android 10 honours this flag regardless of targetSdk 36; Android 11+ ignores it, where it is not needed.
Android 7-10 users then get one storage prompt. If they refuse, step 3 shows the share fallback.

7) Optional, later: a small Capacitor plugin in MainActivity using Intent.ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT (the system "Speichern unter" dialog, no permissions needed) for "Projekt sichern" and "PDF speichern". Write the bytes in chunks instead of one large base64 string, so big section PDFs do not have to cross the bridge in one piece.

8) Verification and honesty:
- Add a vitest test that mocks platform.ts and checks that downloadBlob reports `savedPath` = null when writeFile rejects, and that the UI then shows the failure message, not a path.
- Add a README line saying the Android save behaviour has only been checked from source until it is tested on Android 10 and 13+.

findings.title: Android back button leaves the app from every screen, including open dialogs; in the PWA, back jumps from step 8 to Home
findings.problem: The APK does not include @capacitor/app (package.json; capacitor.plugins.json lists only filesystem and share). Capacitor 8's BridgeActivity has no back handling: there is no OnBackPressedCallback anywhere in @capacitor/android. So the hardware back button or back gesture takes the default Activity path. On Android 12 and newer it sends the app to the background; on Android 7-11 it finishes the activity, which destroys the WebView and restarts the app on Home. Back never closes a dialog and never returns to the previous step. In the browser/PWA, step changes use history.replaceState (Workspace.tsx:23-26) and modals are not in the history, so back always leaves the whole project. Pending saves depend only on visibilitychange/pagehide (useProject.ts:131-141); there is no native pause hook.
findings.evidence: Code: android/app/src/main/java/de/mosaicplan/app/MainActivity.java is an empty BridgeActivity. node_modules/@capacitor/android/.../BridgeActivity.java has no onBackPressed, and grep for OnBackPressed or canGoBack finds only MockCordovaWebViewImpl. android/app/src/main/assets/capacitor.plugins.json contains only Filesystem and Share. Browser reproduction: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/ux-mobile-android/scripts/back.cjs opens a project, computes it, goes to step 8, opens a stone dialog and presses back. Output (.../out/back.txt): 'after BACK #1: http://localhost:4173/ | dialog still open: false | on home: true'. history.length stays 3 across step changes.
findings.proposal: Add @capacitor/app (npx cap sync). Create a small back-handler stack, src/ui/backStack.ts, with a LIFO list and a useBackHandler(fn, active) hook. Modal registers onClose while mounted. Workspace registers 'go to previous step' when idx > 0, and 'go to project list' at step 1. App registers 'go to #/' when route !== ''. In main.tsx, when isNative(): App.addListener('backButton', () => { if (!backStack.run()) App.minimizeApp(); }). Use minimizeApp rather than exitApp so state survives. Also App.addListener('pause', () => flushAll()), where useProject registers its flush in a global set. For the web/PWA: use history.pushState for step changes instead of replaceState, push a {modal} entry when a Modal opens, and close it on popstate. Add an e2e check that page.goBack() with an open dialog only closes the dialog.
corrected:
Use browser history as the single source of truth for both the PWA and the APK.

(1) Workspace: make the step come from the route.
- In Workspace.tsx, replace the `useState` step with a value derived from the route: `const step = isStep(initialStep) ? initialStep : 'photo'`.
- Change `setStep(s)` to `location.hash = '#/project/' + id + '/' + s`. This pushes a history entry, and App's existing hashchange listener re-renders Workspace with the new `initialStep`. Workspace stays mounted because `key` is the project id, so the project is not reloaded.
- Use `history.replaceState` plus a `setHash` call only for the automatic jump to 'preview' after loading (Workspace.tsx:28-31), so that it does not create an extra entry.

(2) Modal (components.tsx:107): give it its own history entry.
- On mount, run once: `history.pushState({ mpModal: true }, '')` (same URL, so no hashchange fires).
- Add a `popstate` listener that calls `onCloseRef.current()`. Keep `onClose` in a ref so the effect does not re-run on every render; the current effect depends on `[props]`.
- When the modal closes through ✕, Escape or the backdrop, call `history.back()` if `history.state?.mpModal` is set, and ignore the resulting popstate.
- Guard against the StrictMode double mount by checking `history.state?.mpModal` before pushing.

(3) Native app:
- `npm i @capacitor/app@^8.1` and `npx cap sync android`.
- In main.tsx, when `isNative()`, add: `App.addListener('backButton', ({ canGoBack }) => canGoBack ? history.back() : App.minimizeApp())`. Hash and pushState entries count in the WebView's canGoBack. Use `minimizeApp`, not `exitApp`, so in-memory state survives.
- Optional hardening: `App.addListener('pause', () => flushAllProjects())`, where useProject registers its `flush` in a module-level Set.

(4) Add e2e checks in e2e/run-e2e.cjs:
- (a) With the stone dialog open, `page.goBack()` closes the dialog, the URL stays on `.../preview`, and the canvas is still visible.
- (b) Going from colors to preview and then `goBack()` shows step 'colors' (the active stepper button and the h2).
- (c) A further `goBack()` leaves the project only after the step history is used up.

Impact 4, effort M.

Use one back mechanism: browser history, the same on web and Android.

(1) Steps controlled by the URL, in Workspace.tsx:
- Add useEffect(() => { if (STEPS.includes(initialStep) && initialStep !== step) setStep(initialStep) }, [initialStep]) so a back or forward traversal updates the screen.
- Make user clicks on the stepper, the Next/Back buttons and the stale badge call goStep(s), which pushes the new hash (location.hash = h, or history.pushState plus setStep).
- Keep replaceState for automatic redirects only, for example the 'preview' jump after loading at Workspace.tsx:28-31, so back never lands on a step the user did not choose.

(2) Modals in history, in components.tsx Modal:
- On mount, run history.pushState({mpModal: id}, '') with the same URL.
- Listen for popstate. When this modal's entry is no longer current, call onClose.
- Have the X button, Escape and a backdrop tap call history.back() instead of onClose; the popstate handler then closes the modal.
- In the cleanup, if the modal unmounts programmatically (for example after Save) and history.state?.mpModal === id, call history.back() so no stale entry is left.
- Keep a module-level depth counter so the nested free-form modal in StoneDialog closes first.

(3) Android:
- Add @capacitor/app@^8.1 (8.1.2 exists, peer @capacitor/core >=8) and run npx cap sync.
- In main.tsx, when isNative(): App.addListener('backButton', ({canGoBack}) => canGoBack ? history.back() : App.minimizeApp()).
- Do not use exitApp, and do not build a separate JS backStack.
- The listener is mandatory: without it, plugin 8.1.2 ignores back at the root.
- Optional: App.addListener('pause', flushAll), where useProject registers its flush in a module-level Set.

(4) Tests: extend e2e/run-e2e.cjs:
- Open the stone dialog, call page.goBack(), and check that the dialog is closed and the URL and active step-* are unchanged.
- Call goBack() again and check that the previous step is shown and the active stepper button matches the URL hash.
- Open the nested free-form modal and check that back closes only the inner modal.
- Check manually on a device or emulator with API 30 and API 34+ that back at Home minimizes the app and that reopening keeps the state.

No changes to src/core, so stone counts and cut dimensions are not affected. Impact 4 (5 on Android 7-11), effort M.

findings.title: Android edge-to-edge: dark status-bar icons over the dark top bar, and modals and page bottom ignore safe areas
findings.problem: With targetSdk 36, viewport-fit=cover (index.html) and Capacitor 8's SystemBars plugin, a WebView of version 140 or newer receives real insets (SystemBars.java:194). The app's navy top bar (#1d2a3a, styles.css:81-92, padding-top env(safe-area-inset-top)) is then drawn behind the status bar. No SystemBars style is configured (capacitor.config.ts), so the DEFAULT style resolves to LIGHT in light mode (SystemBars.java:327-333), which means dark status-bar icons on the dark bar. In system dark mode the navigation bar gets light icons over the light page background. Modals do not use safe-area insets (.modal-backdrop padding 12px, .modal max-height 92vh), and main padding-bottom is a fixed 40px.
findings.evidence: Code: SystemBars.java:39 (WEBVIEW_VERSION_WITH_SAFE_AREA_FIX = 140), :194 (passthrough when WebView >= 140 && viewport-fit=cover), :292 (setAppearanceLightStatusBars(!DARK)), :327 getStyleForTheme(). core-plugins.d.ts:242-262 (Light = 'dark system bar content'). Simulation with CDP Emulation.setSafeAreaInsetsOverride (top 40, bottom 48): /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/ux-mobile-android/scripts/safearea.cjs (output .../out/safearea.txt): 'modal top 34 bottom 810 | status bar ends at 40, nav bar starts at 796'. Screenshot .../shots/m-safearea.png shows the modal top under the status bar and the modal bottom under the navigation bar. The icon colour cannot be verified without a device; it follows from the plugin source.
findings.proposal: In main.tsx, when isNative(): import { SystemBars, SystemBarsStyle, SystemBarType } from '@capacitor/core'; call SystemBars.setStyle({ style: SystemBarsStyle.Dark, bar: SystemBarType.StatusBar }) and SystemBars.setStyle({ style: SystemBarsStyle.Light, bar: SystemBarType.NavigationBar }). In capacitor.config.ts add plugins: { SystemBars: { initialViewportFitValueHint: 'cover' } } to avoid layout jumps. CSS: .modal-backdrop { padding: max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-top)) max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-right)) max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-left)) }, .modal { max-height: calc(100dvh - env(safe-area-inset-top) - env(safe-area-inset-bottom) - 24px) }, main { padding-bottom: calc(40px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) }, and the sticky step bar (separate finding) also uses env(safe-area-inset-bottom).
corrected:
1) src/main.tsx: only when isNative() and the insets really reach the page, call `import { SystemBars, SystemBarsStyle, SystemBarType } from '@capacitor/core'` (all exported in @capacitor/core 8.6.0, dist/index.js:647). To check that the insets reach the page, add a probe element with `padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top)` and read it with getComputedStyle. Read it again on `resize`, or for about 1 s after load, because the plugin calls requestApplyInsets only after onPageCommitVisible. If the probe height is above 0, call `SystemBars.setStyle({ style: SystemBarsStyle.Dark, bar: SystemBarType.StatusBar })` for light icons over the navy .topbar. Then call `SystemBars.setStyle({ style: SystemBarsStyle.Light, bar: SystemBarType.NavigationBar })` for dark icons over the light #f4f1ec page. If the probe is 0, keep DEFAULT. In that case the plugin pads the decor view and the bars sit over the theme's window background, which DEFAULT already handles. The plugin re-applies the explicit style when the configuration changes (SystemBars.java:109-114), so one call is enough.

2) capacitor.config.ts: add `plugins: { SystemBars: { initialViewportFitValueHint: 'cover' } }` so the first layout gets the insets without a jump. Then run `npx cap sync`.

3) src/ui/styles.css:
- `.modal-backdrop`: set `padding: max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-top)) max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-right)) max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-left))`.
- `.modal`: replace `max-height: 92vh` with `max-height: 100%`. The backdrop is position:fixed with inset 0, so 100% is its content height once the padding is subtracted.
- `main`: set `padding-bottom: calc(40px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`.
- Optional: change `.topbar` `padding-top` to `calc(8px + env(safe-area-inset-top))`, so the bar's content does not sit right against the status bar.

4) Check it on a real Android 15 or 16 phone with current WebView, in light and dark mode, with both gesture and 3-button navigation. Also test with the --safe-area-inset-top=0 path, by setting the SystemBars config `insetsHandling: 'native'`.

Impact 3 and effort S stand. The status-bar icon contrast is the part the user will notice. The modal and page-bottom changes are small polish: an overlap of 6-18px, and only with 3-button navigation.

findings.title: No WebView version guard: the bundle needs about Chrome 98+, but Capacitor only checks 60+ and shows nothing when it fails
findings.problem: minSdk is 24 (Android 7). The production bundle uses ??= (Chrome 85), structuredClone (Chrome 98; storage/projects.ts:39 and core/serialize.ts:100), module workers (Chrome 80; workers/client.ts:12), OffscreenCanvas (render.ts) and createImageBitmap imageOrientation. Capacitor's default minWebViewVersion is 60, and without an errorPath it only logs 'System WebView is not supported' (Bridge.java:305-312). On devices with an outdated Android System WebView (no Play updates, old ROMs), the app shows a blank screen or a compute or duplicate action fails, with no explanation.
findings.evidence: node_modules/@capacitor/android/.../Bridge.java:105 (DEFAULT_ANDROID_WEBVIEW_VERSION = 60), :305-312 (errorUrl only if configured). capacitor.config.ts has no android.minWebViewVersion or errorPath. android/variables.gradle: minSdkVersion = 24. Built bundle check: dist/assets/index-JNn1Y7iU.js contains '??=' and 'structuredClone' (node check output: 'has ??=: true structuredClone: true'). Not tested on an old device.
findings.proposal: In capacitor.config.ts set android: { allowMixedContent: false, minWebViewVersion: 100, errorPath: 'webview-update.html' }. Add public/webview-update.html as a static ES5 page in German, English and Turkish: 'Bitte „Android System WebView“ bzw. Chrome im Play Store aktualisieren', with a market://details?id=com.google.android.webview link. As a second guard for the PWA, add a tiny inline script in index.html that checks 'structuredClone' in window && 'OffscreenCanvas' in window and otherwise shows the same message instead of the empty #root.
corrected:
1) Make the browser target explicit in vite.config.ts: `build: { target: ['chrome111','edge111','firefox114','safari16.4'] }`. This matches Vite 8's current default and avoids silent drift on a Vite upgrade. Document "Android System WebView / Chrome >= 111" in the README limitations table.

2) In capacitor.config.ts:
`android: { allowMixedContent: false, minWebViewVersion: 111 }, server: { errorPath: 'webview-update.html' }`
errorPath must go under `server`; Capacitor reads `server.errorPath`. Then run `npx cap sync android`.

3) Add public/webview-update.html as a static ES5 page: no modules, no arrow functions, inline CSS. Capacitor also uses errorPath for generic main-frame load errors, so the page's script parses `navigator.userAgent` for `Chrome/(\d+)`:
- If the version is < 111, show the update text in de/en/tr. German: "Bitte ‚Android System WebView‘ (Android 10+) bzw. ‚Google Chrome‘ (Android 7–9) im Play Store aktualisieren und die App neu starten". Link to `market://details?id=com.google.android.webview` and `market://details?id=com.android.chrome`, with an https://play.google.com fallback. Show the detected version number.
- Otherwise, show a generic "Laden fehlgeschlagen – App neu starten" message.
Pick the language with navigator.language.

4) In index.html, add a classic inline `<script>` before the module script. This covers the PWA, Huawei WebView (whose Capacitor check defaults to 10) and devices that report a misleading version. Probe the real syntax and APIs, not OffscreenCanvas:
`try { new Function('var o={};o.a??=1;o.b||=2;class X{f;static{}}'); if(!('structuredClone' in window)) throw 0; } catch(e) { document.getElementById('root').innerHTML = '…same localized message…'; }`
Keep the guard itself in ES5 syntax.

5) Optional: add a Playwright check that loads index.html with `structuredClone` deleted via addInitScript. Assert that the message appears and the page is not blank.

1. capacitor.config.ts: `android: { allowMixedContent: false, minWebViewVersion: 111 }, server: { errorPath: 'webview-update.html' }`. Note that errorPath goes under `server`, because CapConfig.java:251 reads server.errorPath. 111 matches Vite 8's default chrome111 target. Alternatively, pin `build: { target: 'chrome98' }` in vite.config.ts (with the worker build covered too) and use minWebViewVersion 98. Then run `npm run android:sync` so android/app/src/main/assets/capacitor.config.json picks up the change.

2. public/webview-update.html: a self-contained page with inline CSS, no modules, ES5 only, no app bundle. Text in German first, then English and Turkish:
   - DE: "Ihre Android-WebView ist zu alt. Bitte ‚Android System WebView‘ und ‚Google Chrome‘ im Play Store aktualisieren und MosaicPlan neu starten."
   - Two links: market://details?id=com.google.android.webview and market://details?id=com.android.chrome. On Android 7-9, Chrome is often the WebView provider.
   - An https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=... fallback link.
   Bridge.launchIntent already opens non-app hosts through ACTION_VIEW, so the market: links work. Vite copies public/ into dist, and the local server serves it.

3. index.html (PWA and APK): put a classic, non-module inline script before the module script.
   - It checks `'structuredClone' in window`, `'OffscreenCanvas' in window` and `'createImageBitmap' in window`.
   - It runs a syntax probe: `try { new Function('class A{#a=1;static{}} var b; b??=1;') } catch(e) { fail }`.
   - It checks module-worker support: `var ok=false; try{ new Worker('data:,',{get type(){ok=true;return 'module'}}).terminate() }catch(e){}`.
   - On failure, it replaces #root with the same three-language message and sets a flag. main.tsx then skips createRoot when the flag is set.
   Do not block on OffscreenCanvas alone if render.ts gets a canvas fallback later.

4. README: add a requirements line: "Android 7+ mit aktueller Android System WebView/Chrome (≥111); Browser: Chrome/Edge 111+, Firefox 114+, Safari 16.4+".

5. Test: an e2e case that uses page.addInitScript to delete window.structuredClone, loads http://localhost:4173/, and asserts the update message is visible and #root has no app UI. Nothing here touches src/core, so geometry, counts and cut dimensions stay unchanged.

findings.title: Full-project PDF for big projects crashes the app; section-wise export impossible above 200 sections
findings.problem: For large projects the PDF step only offers 'Alle (N)' because the per-section chips are hidden when there are more than 200 sections (StepPdf.tsx:134). The UI then warns 'Sehr viele Seiten – ggf. Abschnitte einzeln exportieren' (StepPdf.tsx:171), but there is no way to do that. generatePdf puts every page into one in-memory jsPDF document (pdf.ts:83) and builds the whole file at the end with doc.output('arraybuffer') (pdf.ts:877). Memory therefore grows by about 3 MB per 4-sheet A4 section until the renderer runs out. On a phone or the Capacitor WebView, which have smaller heaps, the whole page crashes. The worker client does not detect the crash (client.ts:25 only handles onerror).
findings.evidence: 1000x500 cm, 4 mm tiles, 1 mm joint, 2,003,001 positions, default 30x30 cm sections (578): the UI shows only 'Alle (578)' and 'ca. 2.312 Verlegeblätter', with 0 section chips. Screenshot: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/performance-scale/browser/pdf2m/pdf-step.png; log: .../performance-scale/browser-pdf2m.log. Desktop Chromium: the export succeeds after 33.9 s and gives a 30 MB PDF. The same run with a 1 GB JS heap (--js-flags=--max-old-space-size=1024, roughly a phone/WebView budget) ends in 'Page crashed' after 26.8 s, and the whole tab dies (.../performance-scale/browser-pdf2m-heap1g.log, script browser-pdf-heap.cjs). Node with its default heap (npx tsx bench-pdf.ts 10000 5000 4 1 a4 1): the trace shows heap 27 MB at the cover, then 1,772 MB after section Q34 (all 578 sections drawn at 40 s), then 'FATAL ERROR: ... JavaScript heap out of memory' (.../performance-scale/pdf/res-1000x500-trace.txt). A single section (A1) of the same project works: 4.0 s, 0.5 MB.
findings.proposal: (1) Always offer section selection. Above 200 sections, replace the chips with a compact picker: a range text field ('A1-C4, D7'), row/column selectors, and buttons like 'next 25 sections'. (2) Automatic batching: when the estimated sheet count is over a limit (for example 250, or derived from navigator.deviceMemory), generate a series of PDF files, each with at most K sections and a new jsPDF instance per file, then release the old one. Each file repeats the cover, legend and template index. Sheet IDs are already section-relative (A1-3), so joining marks stay valid across files. (3) Add a pre-flight memory estimate (about 3 MB per A4 4-sheet section at 4 mm, measured here) and block with an explanation instead of crashing. (4) Add a worker watchdog in client.ts: a timeout plus 'messageerror', and treat a vanished worker as an error so the UI shows a message instead of hanging or crashing.
corrected:
1) Always let the user choose sections (StepPdf.tsx:129-152). Keep the chips up to 200 sections. Above that, show the scrollable section grid that StepPlan already renders for all sections (StepPlan.tsx:147-167, gridTemplateColumns repeat(G.scols)) as a multi-select. Add a range text field parsed into `sectionIds` (e.g. "A1-C4, D7"; rows are letters and columns are numbers, as produced by layout.ts IDs) and buttons to select a row or a column. Also add a "PDF {sec.id}" button next to "CSV {sec.id}" in StepPlan.tsx:226. It calls the same runWorker('pdf') with `options.sectionIds=[sec.id]`; a single section is known to work (A1: 4.0 s, 0.5 MB). This directly covers requirement 10 (edit and print sections separately). Change the 'pdfui.many' text in de/en/tr so it names the control that actually exists.

2) Split large exports into parts (the batching approach above was measured to work). In StepPdf, estimate the memory per export from the number of stones in the selected sections. Measured cost: about 0.9 KB of heap per drawn stone (1772 MB / 2.0M stones at A4 1:1), plus output overhead of up to about 2x for the final doc.output string. Budget: `performance.memory?.jsHeapSizeLimit` (Chromium and Android WebView); otherwise `(navigator.deviceMemory ?? 2) * 1024 MB / 4`; otherwise 512 MB. Use about 35% of the budget per file. If the selection is over budget, do not run 'Alle' as one file. Show 'Teil 1/N … Teil N/N' buttons instead, each covering a contiguous run of sections in reading order, generated one at a time on demand. Each part is a separate runWorker('pdf') call, and therefore a separate jsPDF instance. This avoids browser multi-download blocking and keeps only one document in memory. On Android it goes through the existing platform.ts save/share for each part. Each part repeats the cover, legend and template index. Its header shows 'Teil k/N · Abschnitte X–Y', and page numbers count within the part (pdf.ts:866-874 already numbers pages per document). Sheet and section IDs and the joining marks are section-relative, so they stay valid across parts. Do not change any cut dimensions or counts.

3) If even one selected section is over the budget (an extreme tile/section size combination), block it with an explanation such as "Abschnitt zu groß für den Speicher dieses Geräts – Abschnittsgröße im Verlegeplan verkleinern". Do not start the export only to crash.

4) Replace the client.ts watchdog with the following. A worker OOM takes down the whole renderer process, so client.ts cannot observe it; only Android can catch it. In android/app/src/main/java/de/mosaicplan/app/MainActivity.java, register a com.getcapacitor.WebViewListener whose onRenderProcessGone reloads the bridge WebView (or recreates the activity) and returns true. Today Capacitor returns false (BridgeWebViewClient.java:92-103), so Android kills the app. Project data in IndexedDB survives the reload. Optionally write a 'pdf-in-progress' flag to localStorage before the export and clear it afterwards. After a reload, if the flag is still set, show 'Der letzte PDF-Export war zu groß – bitte in Teilen exportieren'.

Ordered by value per effort.

1. Section selection is always available (effort S, the biggest win).
- In StepPdf.tsx, replace the chip row that is capped at 200 (lines 129-152) with the same section grid StepPlan already renders without a cap (StepPlan.tsx:147-167). Move it into a shared SectionPicker component in components.tsx.
- The picker should have:
  - tap to toggle a section;
  - "Zeile"/"Spalte" buttons to select a whole row or column;
  - "Nur offene Abschnitte" (sections with placed < total, from api.progress.perSection);
  - a text field with an exact parser for ranges such as "A1-C4, D7". Unknown IDs are rejected with a message and never silently dropped.
- In StepPlan's section-info (next to "CSV {sec.id}", StepPlan.tsx:222), add a "PDF {sec.id}" button. It sets pdfOptions.sectionIds = [sec.id] and jumps to step 10.
- Add a "Abbrechen" button while busy. It calls cancelChannel('pdf').
- Revoke the previous result URL before creating a new one.

2. Split export with a fresh jsPDF per file (effort M).
- Add a parts option to generatePdf: { global: boolean; sectionIds: string[] | null; partLabel?: string }.
  - Part 0, "Übersicht": cover, images, overview, colour legend, material list, per-shape/per-size tables, cut templates. This is the existing code minus the section loop and the coordinates.
  - Parts 1..n: for each section in the batch, the existing section cover with legend and neighbours, its sheets, and its coordinate pages.
  - Every page header gets "Teil k/n · Abschnitte A1–C24". Page numbers count within the file.
- Template numbers stay global, because collectTemplates keeps scanning the whole project in every part. "(T12)" in a coordinate table therefore still points to the same template in Part 0.
- Batching runs on the main thread. Group sections in row-major order by estimated cost, using the shared planner from step 3.
  - Cost = cellsWithCodes × 1 KB + cellsWithoutCodes × 0.1 KB + coordRows × 5 KB, plus a safety factor of 2. The constants are measured: 0.94 KB per coded cell and 5 KB per coordinate row in V8.
  - The budget is about 35% of performance.memory.jsHeapSizeLimit when available. Otherwise use a conservative fixed budget of 150 MB.
- Run one runWorker('pdf') call per part, one after another, so each jsPDF instance can be garbage-collected. Keep only the ArrayBuffers (about 15 bytes per cell compressed, so 30 MB total for 2M cells).
- Delivery:
  - Web: show a list of download links, one per part. Do not trigger multiple downloads automatically.
  - Native (platform.ts): write every part to Documents/MosaicPlan, then call Share.share once with files: [all uris].
- Keep "Eine Datei" as an option. Show it as the recommended choice only when the estimate fits the budget, which is the PC case.

3. Shared sheet planner (effort S).
- Export planSheets(layout, sections, opts) from pdf.ts. It returns the exact cx/ry split from tilesOf and the cost terms above.
- Both StepPdf (estimate and batching) and generatePdf use it. This removes the PH-53 vs PH-50 mismatch and the difference between rounding in mm and splitting at cells.
- Every number shown before export stays labelled "ca.".

4. Crash recovery instead of a watchdog (effort S).
- Before each PDF worker call, write localStorage 'mp.pdfInFlight' = { projectId, sectionCount, cells }. Clear it on success or error.
- On the next app start, if the flag is still set, show: "Der letzte PDF-Export war zu groß für dieses Gerät – bitte in Teilen exportieren". This message is never shown otherwise.
- On Android, add a WebViewListener in MainActivity whose onRenderProcessGone reloads the bridge and returns true, so the APK is not killed.
- A 'messageerror' handler in client.ts is fine as a one-liner. Skip timeout watchdogs, because legitimate exports already take 30 s or more.

5. Tests in vitest (pdf.test.ts already has a per-colour stone counter).
- The planned batches partition the sections: each section appears exactly once.
- For a project with 6 or more sections, the sum of drawn stones per colour across all part PDFs equals computeStats totals.
- Sheet IDs and join labels in the part PDFs match a single-file export of the same sections.
- The range parser round-trips ("A1-B2" gives A1, A2, B1, B2) and rejects unknown IDs.

findings.title: Failed saves (IndexedDB quota or abort) are only logged to the console, and the user keeps working on data that is not being stored
findings.problem: All debounced saves end in fn().catch(e => console.error('Speichern fehlgeschlagen', e)). Nothing appears in the UI. If storage is full (large projects store photo, mosaic and progress; a 2M-cell project needs about 16 MB of typed arrays per save) or a transaction aborts, the user goes on laying stones and editing for hours, then loses everything on the next reload.
findings.evidence: Repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t7_silent_save_failure.cjs (aborts every IDB write transaction after compute, simulating a QuotaExceededError abort). Output t7_output.txt: 'UI placed = 1.383 | visible error elements: []', console 'Speichern fehlgeschlagen null' (x2), 'after reload: name = Test: Tier (Katze) | placed = 0'. Screenshot t7-no-error-shown.png. Code: useProject.ts:111, Projects.tsx:63-90 (duplicate/export/delete without try/catch), StepPlan.tsx:35-52 (CSV export without catch).
findings.proposal: Add `saveError: string | null` and `dirty: boolean` state to useProject. Set them in schedule()/flush() on rejection (map QuotaExceededError to a localized message) and clear them on the next successful save. Show a persistent red banner in Workspace: 'Änderungen konnten nicht gespeichert werden (Speicher voll?) – [Erneut versuchen] [Projekt exportieren]'. Keep timers for failed keys so the retry writes the current state. Wrap the Projects actions and the CSV export in try/catch with setErr. Optionally warn when navigator.storage.estimate() shows usage > 80 % of quota.
corrected:
1) useProject.ts: add a `failedKeys = useRef(new Set())` plus state `saveError: string | null` and `saving: boolean`. - In schedule(), on rejection: add the key to failedKeys, then `setSaveError(msg(e))`. Map `e?.name === 'QuotaExceededError'` to the i18n key 'save.quota'; everything else goes to 'save.failed' with e.message. On success: remove the key from failedKeys and, if the set is empty, set saveError to null. - Change flush() so it walks the union of Object.keys(saveTimers.current) and failedKeys. Use Promise.allSettled and route each result through the same success/failure handling. That way a retry writes the current in-memory state from recRef and computedRef. - Wrap the pagehide, visibilitychange and unmount calls as `flush().catch(() => {})` so they don't raise unhandled rejections. - Return saveError and a `retrySave = flush` from the hook. 2) storage/projects.ts: split exportProject into `buildProjectExport(rec, img, mosaicWithoutProgress, progress): Promise` and keep exportProject(id) as a thin wrapper that loads from IndexedDB and calls it. In useProject, add `exportCurrent()`. It must build the export from recRef.current, the image state and `packMosaic(computedRef.current.data)` (split into mosaic and progress), NOT from IndexedDB, because IndexedDB holds the stale state while saves are failing. 3) Workspace.tsx: when api.saveError is set, show a sticky `role="alert"` banner above the step content, in de/en/tr. German text: 'Änderungen konnten nicht gespeichert werden (Gerätespeicher voll?). Bitte Projekt sichern.' The banner has two buttons: [Erneut versuchen], which calls api.retrySave, and [Projekt als Datei sichern], which calls exportCurrent() and then downloadBlob. The banner should stay until a save succeeds. 4) Projects.tsx:63-90: wrap duplicate, export and delete in try/catch and pass errors to the existing setErr. For duplicate, map QuotaExceededError to 'save.quota'. StepPlan.tsx exportCsv: add a catch that sets a local error state rendered as `

`, as StepPdf already does. 5) Optional: on Workspace mount, call navigator.storage.estimate(). If usage/quota > 0.8, show a yellow hint that links to Settings, which already has persist() and a usage display. 6) Tests: add an e2e test modelled on v_quota.cjs. It patches IDBObjectStore.put to throw QuotaExceededError and then asserts that: - the banner appears; - after the patch is removed, 'Erneut versuchen' persists the name and progress across a reload; - while the patch is active, the emergency export contains the unsaved progress.

1) useProject.ts: track dirty keys separately from the timers.
- Add `dirty = useRef<Set<'rec'|'mosaic'|'progress'>>()` and state `saveState: 'saved'|'saving'|'error'` plus `saveError: string|null`.
- schedule() adds the key to dirty. A key leaves dirty only after its write has resolved. When the write is rejected, the key stays dirty, saveError is set and an automatic retry is scheduled with backoff (2 s, 5 s, 15 s, 60 s).
- flush() and a new retrySave() iterate over dirty, not over saveTimers. Each always writes the current recRef/computedRef state. On failure they set saveError and do not swallow it (pagehide/visibilitychange/unmount still call `void` on them).
- In compute(): if only the final Promise.all save fails, keep the computed state, mark rec, mosaic and progress dirty, and set saveError instead of computeError. A wrong "compute failed" message must not appear when the mosaic was computed correctly.

2) db.ts: make the connection recoverable.
- In open(), set `db.onclose = () => { dbp = null }` and `db.onversionchange = () => { db.close(); dbp = null }`.
- In tx(), if transaction() throws InvalidStateError, or the result is UnknownError, reset dbp and try once more with a fresh connection.

3) Workspace.tsx:
- Add a small status in ws-head: "Gespeichert" / "Speichert …" / "Nicht gespeichert".
- While saveState === 'error', show a persistent role="alert" banner with mapped messages in de/en/tr:
  - QuotaExceededError: "Speicher voll – Änderungen nicht gespeichert"
  - InvalidStateError or UnknownError: "Verbindung zum Gerätespeicher verloren"
  - anything else: generic message
- Banner buttons: [Erneut versuchen] calls retrySave(). [Sicherung herunterladen] must serialize the IN-MEMORY state (rec, image blob, packMosaic(computed.data) including progress), NOT exportProject(id). To support this, refactor storage/projects.ts into `serializeProject({record,image,mosaic,progress})`, used by both the existing exportProject (which loads from IndexedDB) and the banner.
- While anything is dirty or saveState === 'error', register a `beforeunload` handler (preventDefault) so the browser warns before the tab closes.

4) Wrap the other unguarded writes in try/catch with visible errors:
- Projects duplicate, export and delete (setErr)
- StepPlan exportCsv (add catch with an error message)
- StepPhoto onFile (show "Foto konnte nicht geladen/gespeichert werden")
- Materials saveMaterial/deleteMaterial
- App saveAppSettings

5) Optional, cheap: after the first successful compute, call navigator.storage.persist() once if not yet persisted. Today it is only a manual button in Settings.tsx:50-51. In Settings and the banner, show navigator.storage.estimate() usage, with a warning above 80 %.

6) Tests: add a Playwright case that aborts IndexedDB writes (as in v1). Assert that the banner appears, that the in-memory backup contains the current placed count, and that once writes work again, retrySave() or flush() persists it, so the progress survives a reload.

globalRules:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.
deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.
